goal.original: The user who started this (micha) could not generate because the MPI custom nodes were not installed or updated. Unblock him. Then ship 1.3.1 as a TRUE patch — the only difference from released 1.3.0 being the fix for this case, with none of master's in-flight masking or workflow work.
goal.summary: Root cause found, fixed, and verified LIVE in both directions. The universal-workflow dep set spans two hosts (custom nodes = github.com zips, engineAsset weights = models.cubric.studio) but installed all-or-nothing, and the reject sat ABOVE the custom-node install — so his blocked model host discarded a full set of nodes that downloaded perfectly, on every launch, forever. Fixed on master (0a1d2325, 81bfe1de) and cherry-picked onto branch 1.3.1 (5 commits). 305/305 suites green on master, 301/301 on the branch, eslint clean, release:check passes, notes re-approved. NOT built, NOT tagged, NOT pushed, NOT released.

next_action.description: Build and publish v1.3.1 as a DELTA-ONLY release from branch 1.3.1. Do NOT build from master — master is 45+ commits ahead and carries masking and workflow work that must not ship in a patch. Dispatch the mpi-ci build with ref: 1.3.1 (workflow_dispatch takes a branch, so no tag needs pushing first). CI reads release-baselines/<platform>-<arch>.json and passes --from-manifest automatically, and the branch already carries the 1.3.0 restamp (4d2cbe17), so the delta computes 1.3.0 -> 1.3.1 correctly. Attach only the -update-v1.3.1 bundles to the GitHub Release. Then read the baseline-restamp warning in context.constraints before finishing.

key_decisions: 1.3.1 is built from the maintenance branch 1.3.0, NOT master. This is what makes the patch scope structural rather than a matter of discipline: `git diff v1.3.0 1.3.1` is 18 files, all download/engine/boot/release, zero masking, zero workflows. Verified explicitly because the user asked for it.

The kanban files in 6b27ab4b were deliberately NOT carried onto the branch (board.json, events.jsonl, tasks/MPI-427/). The branch's board is a v1.3.0 snapshot; the card lives on master. They were the only cherry-pick conflicts.

The 71405415 pick dragged six lines into docs/releases/UNRELEASED.md that were never on this lineage — the mask-toolbar Detect entry, which belongs to master's in-flight masking work. Reverted on the branch (d5a01c6b); master keeps it. Scratchpad only, no shipped copy.

Fix 2 uses a NEW event, engine:gate-release, rather than reusing engine:install-skipped. The latter means 'I will use RunPod instead' and MpiRunpodSettings.js:1640 syncs the skip-local-engine switch ON when it fires — reusing it would show the user a local-engine skip they never chose.

Fix 3 fixed the test STUB rather than making the caller defensive. The stub returned the push() index from start() instead of a promise, unlike the real node-downloader-helper API. A stub that lies about the contract hides the whole class of bug.

The shipped 1.3.1 message told users to set DNS to 1.1.1.1. brief.md records that this exact user tested a DNS switch and the download still died at ~20%, and that 1.1.1.1 was pulled from the draft advice before sending. Shipping disproven advice to the users the message exists for was wrong, so the copy now leads with a VPN. This changed a test assertion in transport-error-message.test.cjs.
The mirror was NOT enabled and is NOT in this release. _MODEL_MIRRORS is still empty. The whole point of round 2 is that the app-side fix unblocks the user WITHOUT any Cloudflare change.
constraints: DELTA-ONLY RELEASE — the user's explicit decision this session. CI still produces both the full portable zip and the update bundle in one build (the full stage is what the delta is computed from); shipping delta-only is a PUBLISHING choice about which artifacts get attached.

TRAP that follows from delta-only: release-baselines/*.json must be the FULL portable-stage manifest of the PREVIOUS shipped version (see release-baselines/README.md § Contract). If the 1.3.1 full zip is never published, its manifest must still be captured from the CI build artifact and restamped into release-baselines/, or 1.3.2's delta will silently compute against 1.3.0 and ship fat. Do not skip this because no full artifact was published.

Second delta-only consequence: a NEW user downloading fresh has no full 1.3.1 build. They would get 1.3.0 and then in-app update. The Windows in-app updater was fixed FOR 1.3.0 (see commit 2766f31d, 'the Windows in-app updater is broken pre-1.3.0'), so 1.3.0 -> 1.3.1 in-app is viable. Confirm this is the intended user journey before publishing.

The tag is a BUILD TRIGGER, not a release marker (push: tags: v*). Prefer workflow_dispatch with ref: 1.3.1 so no tag is pushed prematurely. If a tag is pushed, verify `git rev-parse 'v1.3.1^{}'` equals the SHA CI actually built BEFORE publishing — v1.3.0's tag sat 63 commits behind across five rebuild rounds.
